verdicts.why: Solidly built is a property of the thing; the positive sense is the meaning itself, like huge, not an attitude beyond it.
Firm and sure (a strong grip, a strong voice) describes degree of force without approving or disparaging.
Strong medicine or strong coffee names potency of effect; it takes no side on the thing.
Immune to attack (a strong position, strong encryption) is a factual claim about security, not a judgement.
High alcoholic content is a measurable property of the drink with no attitude attached.
A strong scent or trail means recently made; plain description.
Strong verb is a neutral grammatical term of art.
Closeness to the true value is a technical accuracy sense with no attitude toward what it measures.
Beg the question names a logical flaw (assuming the conclusion) in plain idiom; the fault is the referent, not a sneer at the arguer.
Emphatic, authoritative stating describes manner of speech; the narrator's stance toward the speaker is not carried by the verb.
Announcing publicly or officially is a neutral speech act.
Customs declaration is a procedural term with no attitude.
Declaring a dividend is a neutral financial term.
Naming trumps in bridge is a technical game term.
Putting something to the test describes an action without judging the thing tested.
Formal mathematical proof is a neutral technical sense.
Dough rising is plain description of a physical process.
Causing dough to rise with leaven is a baking term with no attitude.
Obtaining probate is a neutral legal term.
Taking a trial impression is a neutral printing term.
Position in time relative to a start or expectation is plain description.
An early stage of development states where something is in a sequence, not what the speaker thinks of it.
Belonging to the distant past (early inhabitants) is neutral chronology.
Expected in the near future (an early reply) is neutral timing.
Early Modern English is a period label with no attitude attached.
